## Phase 2: User Story 1 - Unambiguous repository state (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: Make line endings deterministic and retire only semantically empty,
fully merged residue.

**Independent Test**: A clean checkout and worktree remain clean under the
repository text policy; every retired target has a successful semantic or
ancestry guard recorded in the review.

- [x] T004 [US1] Add deterministic LF and binary exceptions in `.gitattributes`, then verify normalization introduces no semantic source diff.
- [x] T005 [US1] Recheck and retire the exact duplicate typography worktree and local branch, recording guards in `specs/014-framework-health-hardening/review.md`.
- [x] T006 [US1] Recheck and retire merged historical local and remote branches while preserving protected/unmerged refs, recording the exact inventory in `specs/014-framework-health-hardening/review.md`.

**Checkpoint**: `main`, the active branch, tags, user `tmp/` work and every
unmerged ref remain; a second worktree reports no line-ending-only changes.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

- Phase 1 establishes the baseline and blocks every mutation.
- User Story 1 precedes code work so later status is unambiguous.
- User Story 2 is behavior-neutral and can complete before modular extraction.
- T009, T010 and T012 own distinct files and may proceed in parallel; T011
  follows T010 because both change the static orchestrator.
- Generated hash equivalence must be proven before T019 changes dependencies.
- Release tooling and toolchain work must pass before closeout and version bump.
- Archive follows merge; registry publication is the final immutable transition
  from the pushed `main` release candidate.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Complete repository hygiene and historical evidence as the MVP.
2. Land mechanical module extraction with byte-for-byte proof.
3. Add release guards before changing the toolchain.
4. Evaluate stable majors and run the complete closeout matrix.
5. Archive, merge and publish one maintenance release from the exact green
   commit.
